chunks: Yūnus, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sinān, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام.
That he forbade accusing one who is not outwardly known to be outside Islam, unless that is discovered from them; and he said: “The least of what may be the case is that he would have lied.”

key_terms.الْإِسْلَامِ: Islam; the outward religious affiliation under which accusation is not to be made without proof
key_terms.قَذْفِ: slanderous accusation, especially imputing a grave offense
key_terms.كَذَبَ: he lied; the minimum wrongdoing in making an unproven accusation
key_terms.يُطَّلَعَ: to be discovered or established clearly

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about accusing someone without clear proof?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام forbids making accusations against people unless the matter is clearly established from them. The narration emphasizes that, at the very least, a false accuser falls into lying, highlighting the gravity of reckless slander and false attribution.
